title: Recipe file parser
lead: Parse a recipe Markdown file (TOML front matter + sections) into a structured `RecipeDoc`, and serialize it back.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** ingredient line parsing (separate slice); git; DB.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The repo sync, importer and index all depend on parsing one file reliably. Round-trip serialization lets larder write files without breaking them.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body: None if the conventions interview is done.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/recipes/doc.py`
- `tests/fixtures/hugo/` (sample Hugo recipe files the owner provides, under a license compatible with AGPL-3.0)
- `tests/test_recipe_doc.py`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Split the `+++` front matter and parse it with `tomllib`.
2. Walk the Markdown lines to find sections by heading (case-insensitive, trailing colon allowed), per ADR 0018.
3. Collect ingredient list items, keeping raw text and position; keep notes blocks as notes.
4. Return a dataclass `RecipeDoc(slug, front_matter, intro, ingredients, directions, notes, body)`.
5. Serializer: write TOML front matter. Note: stdlib has no TOML writer, so write a minimal writer for the known key types (string, datetime, bool, list of strings).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Parser tests pass on all 3 fixtures.
- After the importer slice, a re-run against the owner's real Hugo recipes parses without errors.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
